title: Hilary of Poitiers (13 January)
hook: a married convert who searched his way into the Church, then took exile rather than sign

segments.voice: Yesterday, Marguerite Bourgeoys, who taught in a stable in early Montreal. Your line was a teacher in the wilderness.

A grown man in Roman Gaul, comfortable, educated, with a household of his own, sits with his books and a question that won't leave him alone: what is a human life for? He has tried the philosophers. Eat well, rest well, live decently. It isn't enough. Then he opens the Jewish scriptures and reaches the burning bush, where Moses asks God's name and hears an answer that is barely a name at all. As a bishop, he will call that moment the turn of his life. His name was Hilary, and he would choose exile over a signature.
screen: `WHAT IS A LIFE FOR?` → `THE BURNING BUSH.` → `A BISHOP WHO WOULDN'T SIGN.`

segments.voice: Hilary tells his own story at the start of his book On the Trinity. God's words to Moses stopped him. In the Douay-Rheims: "I AM WHO AM." Nothing, he writes, could say more about God than that: God simply is. He read on into the Gospels and asked for baptism. Tradition says he already had a wife and a daughter. Later the people of Poitiers made this married convert their bishop. Then the argument arrived. Christians were fighting over whether the Son is truly God, as fully as the Father, or something a step lower. The Emperor favored the bishops who said a step lower, and leaned on the rest to go along and to condemn Athanasius, the bishop of Alexandria who held that the Son is fully God. Hilary would not put his name to it. So he was sent far to the east, into exile. And there, cut off from his church, he wrote. On the Trinity starts from the words of baptism, at the close of Matthew's Gospel: "baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost." His point is simple and stubborn: if that is the name you were baptized into, you don't get to quietly edit it later. Later he came home and kept teaching. Tradition says a man just out of the army came to learn from him, the one the Church remembers as Martin of Tours. The Church later named Hilary a Doctor of the Church. Steady, here, doesn't mean loud. It means the same answer on a good day and in exile.
screen: `I AM WHO AM: A CONVERT'S TURNING POINT.` · `A MARRIED MAN MADE BISHOP.` · `HE WOULD NOT SIGN, SO HE WAS EXILED.` · `IN EXILE HE WROTE ON THE TRINITY.` · then, large: `IN THE NAME OF THE FATHER, AND OF THE SON, AND OF THE HOLY GHOST.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone whose name gets handled carelessly when they aren't in the room, and instead of rehearsing the gossip, find one true, good sentence about them you could say out loud. If you pray, hold that person before God; if you don't, keep their face in mind until the sentence feels steady.
Hilary. A convert and married man made bishop of Poitiers, who chose exile over condemning a fellow bishop, and wrote On the Trinity far from home.
Your line: hilary the steady. Tomorrow, a young man who walks out into the desert. See you then.

howItsDone: Catholics keep Hilary's memorial in January with the Mass and the Liturgy of the Hours, honoring him as a bishop and Doctor of the Church whose writing on the Trinity is still read.

chat.meaning: Hilary, a married convert made bishop of Poitiers, would not condemn Athanasius, was exiled, and wrote On the Trinity there.

notes: Claims rule: no dates spoken (his birth, consecration, exile, death, or his naming as Doctor). Phrygia not named; 'far to the east' instead.
Confirm: On the Trinity Book 1 describes his search and the impact of Exodus 3:14; Book 2 opens from Matthew 28:19.
Wife and daughter: given as 'tradition says' (Venantius Fortunatus; the daughter Abra). Confirm framing.

Exile: tied to his refusal to condemn Athanasius under Constantius II (Council of Béziers). Simplified to 'the Emperor favored the bishops who said a step lower'; confirm the summary is fair to the history and does not overstate.
Martin coming to Hilary is from Sulpicius Severus; confirm chapter.
Index hook in the outline reads 'a married convert, bishop, exile, defender of the Trinity'; script hook line reworded to match the script.
Confirm Douay-Rheims wording of Exodus 3:14 and Matthew 28:19 exactly.
Editor: cut 'great' (unsourced superlative) and 'the older faith' (frames the other side unfairly); now says Athanasius held the Son is fully God.

Audit: Athanasius was not Hilary's friend (no evidence they had met); 'a friend' changed to 'a fellow bishop'. Martin had left the army when he came to Hilary (Sulpicius, Life of Martin 5): 'a soldier' changed to 'just out of the army' / 'ex-soldier'. 'Not a god you could carve or bargain with' was put in Hilary's mouth; now paraphrases De Trinitate 1.5 (nothing more proper to God than to be). Matthew 28:19 was also day 956's verse; now named as the second half of yesterday's line.
Job 2: 'the same closing words of Matthew we heard yesterday' changed to 'at the close of Matthew's Gospel', since day 956 now quotes Luke 1:39, not Matthew 28:19.
